title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The facts available here are limited to the incident title and a single report published by MPR News in August 2026. The article text was not captured, so no details about the lawyer, the cases involved, the citations at issue, or the terms of the suspension can be stated.

The title alone points to a known failure mode: a legal AI tool, or an AI tool used in legal work, producing case citations that do not correspond to real decisions, with those citations then submitted in a legal proceeding. This failure occurs at the point of human use, when a practitioner relies on AI-generated output without independently verifying each citation against an authoritative legal database before filing.

What is not established here is any specific finding about which system was used, whether the lawyer acted knowingly or carelessly, or what the precise scope or conditions of the suspension are, as a news report of a suspension is not a final disciplinary ruling and the article content itself was not available for review.
